## Docker Hub

Docker's official Docker Hub MCP server searches images, inspects tags and repository information, and manages repositories when authenticated. Use it to find an appropriate container image or inspect available image versions before updating a workload. Public content can be queried without credentials.

### Setup

For private repositories or repository management, create a [Docker Hub personal access token](https://docs.docker.com/security/access-tokens/) with the required permissions, supply it as `HUB_PAT_TOKEN`, and pass your Docker Hub username as `-- --transport=stdio --username=<DOCKER_HUB_USERNAME>`. The entry uses stdio inside ToolHive's container, so no OAuth application or upstream HTTP bearer-token configuration is needed. Docker's published image is pinned by digest; see the [upstream setup guide](https://github.com/docker/hub-mcp) for supported tools and authentication. The default `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` setting enables Node to use ToolHive's isolated-network proxy.

tool_definitions.description: Update the details of a repository in the given namespace. Description, overview and status are the only fields that can be updated. While description and overview changes are fine, a status change is a dangerous operation so the user must explicitly ask for it.

description.description: The description of the repository. If user asks for updating the description of the repository, this is the field that should be updated.

full_description.description: The full description (overview)of the repository. If user asks for updating the full description or the overview of the repository, this is the field that should be updated.

status.description: The status of the repository. If user asks for updating the status of the repository, this is the field that should be updated. This is a dangerous operation and should be done with caution so user must be prompted to confirm the operation. Valid status are `active` (1) and `inactive` (0). Normally do not update the status if it is not strictly required by the user. It is not possible to change an `inactive` repository to `active` if it has no images.
